title: Accept 3000018: A modular-storage proof of NP-completeness for chip-firing halting on simple digraphs
body:
## Accepted result and published preprint **A modular-storage proof of NP-completeness for chip-firing halting on simple digraphs**, Alec Kriebel. Published paper and verification package: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23431716 (https://zenodo.org/records/23431716).

A complete attributed proof that ordinary conservative chip-firing HALTING is NP-complete under deterministic polynomial-time many-one reductions on finite loopless simple strongly connected digraphs with nonnegative binary configurations. Hardness holds with polynomial numerical total initial chips and a specified root whose deletion leaves an acyclic graph with no path of two arcs. The main construction permits antiparallel arcs; a separately proved oriented construction forbids them. The proof includes actual legal checkpoints, conservation, schedule-independent least action, polynomial output bounds, all preprocessing cases and a polynomial-bit NP certificate.

The literal modular-bank formula and parallel primed-toppler mechanism are credited to Holroyd, Levine and Winkler, Abelian logic gates, arXiv:1511.00422v2, Lemma 4.1. The prime Boolean and local clause-product encoding is credited to Stockmeyer and Meyer, STOC 1973, Theorem 6.1, and its reconstruction by Gregor Gramlich alone, MFCS 2003, Fact 3. The allowed-predicate intersection is the complement of the classical invalid-variable or failed-clause union; extra local nonBoolean clause-complement residues are already variable-invalid. Neither ingredient nor avoiding global-period expansion is claimed as new. NP membership, capacity and the root-last viewpoint are prior Farrell-Levine/Farrell methods, and long simple-graph clocks are prior Eriksson. Full-result, conservative simple/oriented realization and remaining method priority, and preexisting worldwide openness, remain UNKNOWN after a bounded audit.

AI tools were used extensively in solving, verification, source comparison, programming and writing. This is an unrefereed preprint, without external human peer review, journal acceptance or formal proof-assistant certification. No firstness is claimed. The support ZIP contains the complete TeX source, exact authored historical snapshots, bibliographic hashes/read scopes and fresh standard-library finite diagnostics with meaningful faults. No third-party source bodies are redistributed, no omitted historical program is claimed replayed, and finite tests do not certify the unbounded proof or the literature.

## Accepted scope and review Halting conservative chip-firing on finite loopless simple strongly connected digraphs with nonnegative binary chips is NP-complete; 3-SAT reduction has polynomial total chips and root deletion depth≤1 DAG. Separate appendix proves oriented no-antiparallel version. No original simple-directed-halting gap asserted; unary chip encoding also hard because polynomial chips. Membership credited to Farrell–Levine. No Eulerian-multigraph halting conclusion or conflation with 3000016 reachability. The result is accepted at the exact audited head `f37a3ff66595fcf75bb18bf859be8594c3662242`. 2 fresh independent complete AI whole-package reviews were completed, with the final review finding zero actionable issues. Subsequent bounded administrative adoption is recorded in the current external ROOT final seal; earlier status/counter/hold fields remain dated history. Prior mathematical results and proof dependencies are credited. Historical novelty and worldwide current openness are unestablished. AI tools were used extensively; this is an unrefereed preprint, without conventional human peer review or formal proof certification. The repository Zenodo uploader verified the exact reviewed metadata and PDF/support bytes. The Google Workspace CLI recorded the DOI/details in the requested tracker with exact read-back. No GitHub release is created. Current audit and publication receipts: `audits/pr1098_3000018`.
Preserved original PR description: dated submission history ## Accepted complete theorem and separate oriented strengthening Halting of nonnegative configurations on finite loopless simple strongly connected conservative digraphs is NP-complete under polynomial-time many-one reductions. Target: 3000018 / AMR-029-0018. The separately accepted appendix proves the same theorem for oriented graphs, with no antiparallel arcs. In both constructions, deleting the specified root leaves a DAG of depth at most one, and all initial chip counts, including their total, are polynomially bounded in the SAT input length. Hardness also holds with unary chip encoding. The complete analytic proof preserves the modular-bank identity, Boolean/CRT clause predicates, actual simple graph construction, legal checkpoint schedule and least action, every graph/bit/chip bound, fixed trivial cases, and a self-contained NP membership certificate with the necessary additive one slack. The appendix preserves its separate three-part oriented graph construction and directed three-cycle preprocessing. Aggregate finite checks are supporting metadata only; no omitted executable is needed by the proof. NP membership and the stable-capacity observation are credited to Farrell–Levine, CoEulerian graphs, Section 3 and PDF page 2: https://arxiv.org/abs/1502.04690v3 . Their Section 3.1 poses the simple case, as does the original attributed Egres question: https://oldlemon.cs.elte.hu/egres/open/Complexity_of_the_halting_problem_for_simple_digraphs . This does not resolve Eulerian-multigraph halting and is separate from multigraph reachability for problem 3000016. ## Distribution and review limits Exactly nine authored proof/appendix/audit/acceptance/status and public-source review or metadata files are added under `unsolved_math_prioritization/attempts/3000018/`. Editorial changes reconcile acceptance, use public file names, distinguish historical supporting observations, and bind the distributed mathematical files exactly. All analytic arguments, edge cases and qualifications remain. This AI-assisted, unrefereed edition makes no first-in-literature or exhaustive-current-openness claim, and no external human peer-review, journal-acceptance, or formal proof-assistant-certification claim. Programs, raw generated outputs, datasets, copied third-party source bodies/PDFs/images, and private coordination material are excluded. Edition preparation claims no new scholarly retrieval, source-file rehash, source inspection, literature search, or mathematical test rerun. QUEUE.md and unrelated entries remain unchanged. Editorial preparation adds no substantive proof turn and resets no historical accounting. No merge, release, DOI or outside outreach is requested. Base commit: `f6caddda8f8be2cdb3e91494325d8f7f365bc3fc`. ## Exact distributed file identities - `ACCEPTANCE.json`: 3,457 bytes; SHA-256 `ab41c82fd3dec23912bba4c3669483b454434583d05be825857d720617fd7b89`. - `MANIFEST.json`: 1,846 bytes; SHA-256 `3fe3ecb307b8ef632594269043750d4535eadac6af77096f5555b8029e7fce82`. - `MATHEMATICAL_AUDIT.md`: 17,171 bytes; SHA-256 `6028ff452fa6e49a1cc85a9a01106494dc82c771c4679666e1e602680aa89802`. - `MATHEMATICAL_REPORT.md`: 13,502 bytes; SHA-256 `ca97098b22a3841876d3a9f6d66460312b5820cea1f0cacd381e3d16e6abe4c7`. - `ORIENTED_APPENDIX.md`: 2,692 bytes; SHA-256 `4550676ad4a0af003ba6ce068c2c63f1c4dabba4840af48b2087adbac6921a73`. - `README.md`: 4,559 bytes; SHA-256 `142cba90aaea10baabcba543cbace622940f14b4dd27c490d3982cfc5a7f0892`. - `SOURCE_METADATA.json`: 5,211 bytes; SHA-256 `e3b621919293bca1b78f20f1ec378345814bae0cef70bba54732d33f88353ca0`. - `SOURCE_REVIEW.md`: 4,720 bytes; SHA-256 `3260858a28a5196690283ea9f00dd0136c1b3137ff58ba14b419e947c88cea44`. - `STATUS.json`: 2,311 bytes; SHA-256 `e236b9fe7da5364c06d5e5dc73123d1327eac4f2eb3ae0c1694023453614ec20`.
